enonce_markdown: Day and night are caused by the:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Distinguish the two movements of the Earth: rotation (spinning on its axis) and revolution (travelling round the sun).

### Solution

The Earth **rotates** on its axis once in about 24 hours, so each place turns in turn towards the sun (day) and away from it (night). Revolution and the tilt of the axis cause the seasons, not the alternation of day and night.

**Answer: c.**

enonce_markdown: The Earth takes about how long to complete one revolution round the sun?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

One revolution defines the year; one rotation defines the day.

### Solution

One revolution takes about **365 1/4 days**, which is why one day is added to February every fourth year. 24 hours is the time of one rotation.

**Answer: d.**

enonce_markdown: The Earth turns through 360 degrees in 24 hours. A town lies on longitude 75 degrees West. When the time at Greenwich (GMT) is 18:00, the local time in the town is:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The Earth turns 15 degrees of longitude per hour. Places to the west of Greenwich are behind GMT; places to the east are ahead.

### Solution

Time difference = 75 / 15 = 5 hours. The town is in the west, so it is behind GMT: 18:00 - 5 h = **13:00**.

16:45 comes from treating 75 as minutes; 18:00 ignores the longitude; 23:00 comes from adding 5 hours instead of subtracting them.

**Answer: a.**

enonce_markdown: Cameroon lies between about 2 degrees and 13 degrees North of the equator. Explain why the length of the day varies very little during the year in Cameroon, while it varies much more in a country near the Arctic Circle.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The tilt of the Earth's axis makes the part of each parallel lit by the sun change during the year; the effect is small at the equator and large near the poles.

### Solution

Near the equator, the circle separating day from night (the circle of illumination) cuts every parallel almost into two equal halves throughout the year, so the day lasts about 12 hours in Cameroon in every month. Near the Arctic Circle, the tilt of the axis (23.5 degrees) makes the circle of illumination cut the parallels unequally: in summer a large part of the parallel is in light (very long days), and in winter only a small part (very short days). The nearer to the poles, the greater the difference.

enonce_markdown: On 23 September the sun is overhead at noon on the:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The overhead sun moves between the Tropic of Cancer (21 June) and the Tropic of Capricorn (22 December), crossing the equator at the equinoxes.

### Solution

On 23 September (the September equinox) the sun is overhead at the **equator**, and day and night are equal everywhere. The Tropic of Cancer receives the overhead sun on about 21 June, the Tropic of Capricorn on about 22 December.

**Answer: b.**

enonce_markdown: A ship's clock shows local time 09:20 at the moment when the time at Greenwich is 12:00 (GMT). Find the longitude of the ship, stating whether it is East or West. Show your working.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The Earth rotates 360 degrees in 24 hours, so 15 degrees of longitude correspond to 1 hour (1 degree to 4 minutes). A local time behind GMT means west, a local time ahead means east.

### Solution

Time difference = 12:00 - 09:20 = 2 h 40 min = 160 minutes.

Longitude difference = 160 / 4 = 40 degrees (check: 2 h 40 min = 8/3 h and 8/3 x 15 = 40).

The local time is behind GMT, so the ship is to the west of Greenwich.

**Answer: longitude 40 degrees West.**
